articles.title: 'Exceptional courage': Pilots body writes to PM Modi, requests bravery award for Smit Machchhar
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Federation of Indian Pilots (FIP) wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday seeking an appropriate national bravery award for
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Federation of Indian Pilots (FIP) wrote to Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday seeking an appropriate national bravery award for flydubai pilot Captain Smit Machchhar, citing his “exceptional courage” and professional conduct during the mid-air emergency on September 30.The pilots' body said Machchhar, the pilot-in-command of flydubai flight FZ1073, was reportedly attacked by the first officer with a crash axe and sustained serious injuries during the Dubai-Tel Aviv flight.Despite being injured, Machchhar continued to discharge his responsibilities as pilot-in-command, maintained control of the aircraft and ultimately diverted it safely to Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, FIP said."The Federation of Indian Pilots respectfully submits that acts of exceptional courage such as this deserve recognition at the highest appropriate level. We therefore request the Hon'ble Prime Minister's Office to kindly consider Capt. Smit for an appropriate National Bravery Award / national civilian recognition, in accordance with the applicable Government of India provisions and after due verification of the facts by the competent authorities," it said in a letter."Capt. Smit's actions demonstrate that, even when confronted with grave personal danger and serious injury, the responsibility of a true professional pilot remains firmly centred on the safety of those entrusted to his care," the pilots body said.The organisation noted that 174 passengers and eight crew members were onboard the flight and said Machchhar's actions under extreme personal danger contributed to bringing the aircraft safely to an alternate airport.FIP's appeal comes after Rajya Sabha MP Milind Deora also wrote to PM Modi, urging the government to consider Machchhar for the Ashoka Chakra. Deora said the Mumbai-born pilot's actions demonstrated “courage, selflessness and duty” in an extreme situation.ALSO READ: 'Terrorist act': UAE official on flydubai attack, praises India pilot Smit MachchharMachchhar was allegedly attacked by his co-pilot during the flight, following which passengers and other crew members intervened. The aircraft had transmitted emergency signals and rapidly lost altitude before being diverted to Saudi Arabia.The UAE has ordered an investigation into the incident, including the circumstances, motives and any possible links to terrorist activity or prior planning.PM Modi has also spoken to Machchhar over a video call and praised his courage, presence of mind and composure during the incident.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: 500-computer lab unveiled at IIT-Patna
articles.summary: IIT-Patna inaugurates 500-computer digital hub in Central Library, built with internal resources, serving as digital library and secure exam centre.
articles.body: Patna: IIT-Patna (IIT-P) on Friday unveiled a 500-computer state-of-the-art laboratory, strengthening its digital academic infrastructure. Inaugurated by IIT-P director Amit Patra on Gandhi Jayanti, the facility has been set up inside the institute’s Central Library and is equipped with 500 high-performance computers and advanced networking systems.The entire facility was conceptualised and executed using the institute’s internal resources, without relying on an externally executed infrastructure project. After inaugurating the lab, Patra inspected the hardware, networking and other technical arrangements and discussed its proposed academic applications.The facility has been designed for two functions. During regular academic activities, it will operate as a large-scale digital library, providing students and researchers access to global e-journals, academic databases and digital learning resources.During examinations, the facility will be converted into a 500-terminal digital examination centre, enabling IIT-P to conduct computer-based examinations on a large scale in a controlled and secure environment.The dual-purpose facility is expected to expand access to digital academic resources while providing dedicated infrastructure for technology-driven assessments. articles.title: Gandhi Jayanti: Mamata says stronger India must be guided by Bapu’s ideals
articles.summary: The former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee on Friday said that every step towards building a stronger India should be guided by the ideals of
articles.body: The former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee on Friday said that every step towards building a stronger India should be guided by the ideals of Mahatma Gandhi.In a social media post marking Gandhi Jayanti, Banerjee paid tribute to the Father of the Nation and recalled his enduring message of truth, simplicity and service.She said the country’s journey towards becoming stronger should continue to be guided by Gandhi’s principles, as per PTI report.Trinamool Conngress MP Abhishek Banerjee also paid tribute to Mahatma Gandhi, saying he reaffirmed his commitment to the timeless values of truth, non violation, compassion, justice and equality associated with the father of the Nation.In a social media post, Abhishek Banerjee said Gandhi envisioned an India where every citizen could live with dignity, the most vulnerable had a voice, and the welfare of all Indians remained central to public life.He said that at a time when, in his view, the values of the Republic were being tested, remembering Gandhi should involve standing up for truth, defending justice and safeguarding the dignity and rights of citizens.The Diamond Harbour MP said the most meaningful tribute to Gandhi would be to build an India where all citizens are treated equally, no voice is silenced, no one is left behind and the Constitution remains the guiding force.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Forest dept identifies animal corridors
articles.summary: Jharkhand forest dept identifies 75 wildlife corridors for elephants and big cats, planning habitat improvements to reduce man-animal conflict and aid connectivity.
articles.body: Ranchi: The Jharkhand forest department has identified 75 wildlife corridors used by elephants and big cats and is working on measures to improve their habitats and reduce their movement into human habitats, in an attempt of curb man- animal conflict in the state, principal chief conservator of forests (PCCF) Sanjeev Kumar said.Kumar inaugurating the 72nd Wildlife Week at the forest headquarters here on Friday said that the department was studying ways to ensure that wildlife could continue to live in its natural habitat while development takes place around it.“Whenever we talk about wildlife, we talk only about big animals and their conflict with humans. But we must think about their coexistence. Conflicts arise from the gap between development and nature. The department has been working on improving wildlife habitats and reducing the movement of animals into human habitats,” he said.Kumar said wildlife conservation should not be restricted to large animals such as elephants and big cats. As part of the wildlife week celebrations, the department will organise a workshop on the identification, protection and management of wildlife corridors on Oct 6.Chief conservator of forests S R Natesh, in his address during the event said Jharkhand has around 30% forest area and nearly 40% forest cover. He said railway infrastructure has created gaps in forest connectivity, but the department is in discussions with railway officials to address the issue.Natesh said Jharkhand’s tribal culture has traditionally had a preservation-oriented attitude towards nature.The inaugural programme was attended by a large number of school and college students. Amritesh Kumar, a student of Ranchi Veterinary College, said he was happy to attend the programme as wildlife conservation is closely connected with his field. “I am extremely happy to come to the programme. Since this is also related to our field, it will be useful when I enter professional services,” he said.Stay updated with the latest Ranchi news. Download the TOI App.
